page: Microsoft Azure D32ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running under Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, reaching clock speeds of 4.2 GHz. The memory configuration provides 128.0 GB of RAM, establishing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. In addition, the instance includes an integrated 1888 GB local NVMe SSD and features an expansive 480 MB L3 cache alongside vector and matrix extensions such as AVX-512, Intel AMX (tile and int8), and VAES.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate high throughput for compute and memory tasks. The instance demonstrates top-tier single-threaded compression performance, scoring 36.5 GB/sec in gzip benchmarks and 2232.0 in Geekbench single-core execution. Multi-core Geekbench achieves 18166.0, while static web serving throughput reaches 59.6 GB/sec. Large-block memory tests show read bandwidth of 166.74 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 65.26 GB/sec. In contrast, standard stress-ng benchmarks and raw memory scores remain in the average tier.

The bundled 1888 GB NVMe drive offers qualitative cost efficiency by removing the immediate requirement for external block storage to support temporary caching or scratch space. Tradeoffs include the absence of dedicated GPU hardware for intensive machine learning training and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The D32ds_v7 is technically aligned with production relational databases, Redis cache nodes, web application serving, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and containerized microservice platforms.
description: The Microsoft Azure D32ds_v7 is a general-purpose instance powered by a 32-vCPU Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at up to 4.2 GHz across 16 physical cores. Configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, the instance maintains a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio alongside an integrated 1888 GB NVMe SSD for fast local storage. Benchmark results show strong single-threaded performance, reaching top-tier results in gzip compression at 36.5 GB/sec and a Geekbench single-core score of 2232.0, aided by AVX-512 and Intel AMX hardware extensions. Uncached memory reads reach 166.74 GB/sec, while static web serving yields 59.6 GB/sec throughput. Without hardware accelerators or bundled public IPv4 addresses, the configuration balances dense CPU capacity with fast ephemeral storage. This hardware profile suits production enterprise web applications, relational database hosting, software compilation, batch processing, and distributed microservices.
